_comment: OSF registration update 2 for osf.io/ab2wn: amendments 2-8 from docs/protocol_prisma_p.md. Each value replaces that question's answer. Filed with scripts/osf_update.py; the admin must approve it in OSF before it becomes part of the record.
_justification: Amendments 2-8, all logged with dates and reasons in docs/protocol_prisma_p.md and all made before the stage they affect. (2) SEARCH: eight known 2026 harness papers matched the harness block but not the LLM block, so the LLM block is waived for seven strong harness terms; the search was then frozen on 2026-09-16 at 50,724 raw records and 27,747 candidates, with known-item recall 46/48. (3, 4) SCREENING: no second human screener was available and the single author could not screen 27,747 records, so screening is fully automated and validated rather than human-made: three independent model votes at title/abstract, and at full text an evidence-bundle reading by one model with a stronger model re-reading every exclusion and every low-confidence decision plus a 10% audit of includes. This is a deviation from the registered dual human screening and from current Cochrane/RAISE guidance, and is reported as such, with the framework and its validation presented as a methodological contribution. (5) CODABILITY: judging codability from a paper alone excluded 11 of 15 reference systems, so a record is now read as an evidence bundle (paper, repository at a pinned release, official documentation) and the 19-of-38 codability rule moved from screening to coding. (6) CODED SET: full-text screening yielded a census of 6,162 systems against the 150-300 planned, so the coded set is stratified with known sampling rates (866 high-visibility systems coded completely, 150 of 661 peer-reviewed-only, 100 of 4,635 remaining) and census proportions are reported as weighted estimates. Codability is deliberately not a stratum criterion: requiring it would have dropped 11 of 27 reference systems. (7) SUPPLEMENTARY SEARCH: an independently built pipeline given the same definition and criteria retrieved 103 included records our frozen search never found, so they enter as a PRISMA 2020 'identified via other methods' arm; the same check also measured our title stage against an external screener (agreement 0.84, kappa 0.66). (8) EVIDENCE LOCATORS: the evidence bundle presents repository excerpts without their original line numbers, so a coder cannot cite a real line; repository locators are 'path@commit' and the verbatim quote, verified character-for-character against the exact text the coder was given, is the primary evidence for each cell.
376-12: Searching, screening and system grouping are complete; coding is in progress. The search was frozen on 2026-09-16 (50,724 raw records, 27,747 candidates after deduplication). Title/abstract screening closed 2026-09-18 and full-text screening closed 2026-09-20: 9,967 records sought at full text, 8,435 assessed, 7,085 included, grouped into 6,162 systems. Coding of the stratified coded set (1,116 systems) is under way. All counts are in data/prisma_counts.json in the companion repository.
376-32: Claude (Anthropic) models run through the Claude Code command line in headless mode, for the screening votes, the full-text readings and the coding pass; Elicit, for an independent supplementary search and screening cross-check; Zotero with Better BibTeX (bibliography); Python 3.14 with pandas, jsonschema, rapidfuzz, scikit-learn, statsmodels and matplotlib (validation and synthesis); GitHub Actions for continuous validation of the dataset. Rayyan and ASReview were prepared but are not used, because screening no longer has human screeners to coordinate (amendments 3 and 4); the screening decisions and every quote behind them are instead published as a per-record audit page. All scripts are versioned in the companion repository.
376-48: Include if all of: (a) the source describes a system that wraps an LLM in a loop with tools or an environment; (b) the system's first public release is between 2022-10-01 and 2026-08-31; (c) the paper or documentation is available in English. Exclude: training or reinforcement-learning-only work with no harness description (recorded in a side table where it changes the harness); embodied robotics; benchmarks with no reference harness (recorded for the outcomes table only); single-prompt systems without a loop; components that implement one clause without the loop (sandboxes, tool or protocol specifications, skills packs, tracing SDKs); frameworks with no shipped default agent; duplicate descriptions of one system (the canonical description is kept and the rest are linked). Amendment 5: the registered requirement to code at least 50% of dimensions (19 of 38) is no longer applied at screening. Judging it from a paper alone excluded 11 of 15 reference systems, including ReAct, CodeAct, AutoGen, MetaGPT, Reflexion and OS-Copilot, all of which are codable from their repositories; the rule is enforced at coding, when the pinned artifact is in hand, and the codability estimate recorded at screening is reported but not decisive.
376-46: Technical reports and documentation from major labs and vendors (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta, DeepSeek, Alibaba/Qwen, Cognition, Cursor, Replit and others), agent leaderboards (HAL, SWE-bench, OSWorld, WebArena, Terminal-Bench, GAIA, tau-bench) for system entries and the outcomes table, and curated lists maintained alongside the competing surveys (Awesome-Agent-Harness, Awesome-Agent-Engineering). Amendment 7 adds a supplementary independent search, reported as the PRISMA 2020 'identified via other methods' arm: an independently built systematic-review pipeline (Elicit) was given the same definition and eligibility criteria and ran its own searches, screening 987 records and including 411. Of those, 103 were absent from our frozen candidate set and 102 were absent from the entire raw harvest; all 103 were retrieved and screened by the same full-text procedure, and 37 were included. The same comparison measured our own title stage: on the 434 records both pipelines held, agreement was 0.84 and Cohen's kappa 0.66, and of the 62 records the independent pipeline included but ours excluded at title stage, 10 were recovered on full-text reading and 52 were confirmed excluded.
376-50: Concept blocks combined with AND (OR within a block). Harness block (v2): "agent harness" OR harness OR "agent scaffold*" OR "agentic framework" OR "agent framework" OR "LLM agent*" OR "LM agent*" OR "language agent*" OR "AI agent*" OR "computer agent*" OR "multi-agent" OR "tool-use agent" OR "coding agent" OR "software engineering agent" OR "computer-use agent" OR "GUI agent" OR "web agent" OR "multi-agent framework" OR "agent orchestration" OR "LLM orchestration". LLM block: "large language model" OR LLM OR "foundation model" OR "language model agent". Amendment 2 (v3', 2026-09-16, before screening): the LLM block is waived for seven strong harness terms ("agent harness", "agent scaffold*", "agentic framework", "agent framework", "tool-use agent", "coding agent", "software engineering agent"), because eight known 2026 harness papers matched the harness block but not the LLM block; measured on arXiv this adds 593 records. A nine-term variant was tested and rejected: adding "GUI agent*" and "computer-use agent" pulled in model-training papers. Optional structure block, applied only to the two largest sources (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex) for precision: "tool call*" OR "function call*" OR "control loop" OR "context management" OR memory OR sandbox OR verification OR retry OR planning. Date filter 2022-10-01 to 2026-08-31. GitHub: topic:llm-agent OR topic:ai-agent OR topic:coding-agent, stars:>500, created:>=2022-10-01, followed by README keyword filtering. Amendment history: v1 (registered 2026-09-16) achieved known-item recall 3/12 on the test run; per the registered validation procedure (recall below 90% triggers broadening before screening) it was broadened to v2 (11/12), then to v3' as above. The search was frozen 2026-09-16 at 50,724 raw records and 27,747 candidates, with final known-item recall 46/48 (the two misses are outside the date window). Final per-source strings and hit counts are in data/raw/search_log.md.
376-68: Stage 1: title and abstract (or README summary for repository-only entries). Stage 2: full text, read as an evidence bundle (amendment 5) comprising the paper with its reference list removed, the repository at its last release on or before the freeze date, and official documentation. A record whose documents cannot be retrieved is recorded not_retrievable and reported in the PRISMA flow rather than being decided from its abstract.
376-70: Stage 1 shows title, abstract, year, venue and URL. Stage 2 shows the evidence bundle. Since screening is automated (amendments 3 and 4), there are no human screeners to blind: each model vote is produced independently, in a separate call that cannot see the other votes, and the prompt version used for each vote is recorded per record. Author names are not hidden, because they are needed to identify duplicate descriptions of one system.
376-74: The screening procedure, the harness definition and the twelve-step full-text decision procedure are in docs/protocol_prisma_p.md, docs/definition.md and docs/screening_framework.md in the companion repository, together with the exact prompts and their version identifiers. Screening is inclusive at stage 1: a record without a two-of-three majority is forwarded to full text rather than excluded.
376-78: Amendments 3 and 4 replace dual human screening with automated screening plus validation, because no second screener was available and one person could not screen 27,747 records. Stage 1: every record receives three independent model votes (two different models on the same prompt, then a decisive binary third vote on unsettled records); model-model agreement is reported (kappa 0.56 three-class, 0.62 binary). Stage 2: one model reads every evidence bundle and applies the twelve-step procedure with a verbatim quote for each step it reaches; a stronger model then independently re-reads every exclusion and every low-confidence decision, plus a 10% random audit of includes, so no record is excluded on a single reading. 3,075 records carry two independent full-text readings, and their agreement is reported. No human adjudicated any decision; agreement statistics therefore measure consistency between models, not correctness, and recall against a reference set of known harness systems is the external accuracy estimate (27 of 27 retained).
376-80: At stage 1 a record without a two-of-three majority, or flagged unsure, is forwarded to full text rather than reconciled: the inclusive direction is the safe one when the next stage reads the full evidence. At stage 2 the stronger model's reading is decisive where the two readings disagree, and each disagreement is kept with both readings and both sets of quotes. Every decision, its deciding step and its quotes are logged in data/screening/ and published as a per-record audit page (screening/fulltext_audit.html).
376-82: Screening is a census of all records returned by the frozen search plus snowballing, with no sampling: 6,162 systems were included, far more than the 150-300 expected at registration. Coding is therefore stratified rather than exhaustive (amendment 6), with known rates so that census-level proportions remain estimable: stratum H (a repository with 500 or more stars at freeze, or catalogued by a prior harness survey, or a vendor or major-lab product) holds 866 systems and is coded completely; stratum P (not in H but described in a peer-reviewed paper with a public implementation) holds 661, of which a random 150 are coded (weight 4.41); stratum O (the remainder) holds 4,635, of which a random 100 are coded (weight 46.35). 1,116 systems are coded in total, the sampling seed and per-system assignment are published in data/coding_frame.csv, and strata are reported separately as well as pooled. Codability is deliberately not a stratum criterion: requiring the codability flag recorded at screening would have dropped 11 of the 27 reference systems.
376-84: The registered design followed PRISMA 2020 and Cochrane guidance for dual human screening. That design proved infeasible for a single author on 27,747 records, so screening is fully automated (amendments 3 and 4). This is a deviation from the 2025 Cochrane/Campbell/JBI position statement and RAISE guidance, which treat an LLM as a second screener at most, and it is reported as a deviation rather than presented as compliance. In its place the review supplies the validation such guidance exists to secure: three independent votes at title stage with reported agreement; two independent readings of every exclusion at full text; quoted evidence for every decision, mechanically checked to be verbatim; recall against a reference set of known harness systems with Wilson intervals; an independent second pipeline given the same criteria as an external check on both search recall and screening decisions; and a public per-record audit page. The screening framework and its measured limitations are reported as a methodological contribution of the review.
376-86: Screening votes, the tier assignments, kappa reports, the reference-set recall check, the PRISMA flow counts and the per-record audit page are versioned in the companion GitHub repository and released publicly with the dataset under CC BY 4.0. The exact prompts and their version identifiers are released with them, so any decision can be re-derived.
376-88: Not used. ASReview active-learning prioritization and its stopping rule were registered for a human screener working through a ranked list; with automated screening every record is read at stage 1, so no prioritization or stopping rule is needed and none is applied. Nothing is left unscreened on the basis of a ranking.
376-94: Stage 1: pilot, 30 systems coded twice independently by two model readings on schema v0. Stage 2: per-dimension kappa between the two readings; dimensions below 0.6 are redefined or dropped; schema frozen as v1 with a changelog. Stage 3: coding of the stratified coded set (amendment 6), in two passes: pass A reads the whole evidence bundle and returns all 38 dimensions with a verbatim quote and a locator per cell; pass B re-reads only the cells pass A left unresolved, invalid or without a verbatim quote, using targeted windows of the same bundle. A deterministic 20% sample is coded a second time, independently, for per-dimension reliability. Stage 4: outcomes extraction from papers and leaderboards. A system enters the released dataset only when all 38 of its cells are resolved: either a value of the right shape for its dimension, or an explicit not_reported meaning the sources were read and are silent.
376-100: Coders are not masked to system identity (impossible when reading source code). The reliability subset is selected by a published deterministic rule and coded a second time in a separate call that cannot see the first reading's values.
376-102: Cohen's kappa per dimension on the pilot (30 systems) and on the reliability subset (20% of the coded set), computed between the two independent readings and reported in the manuscript and in the dataset release. Because both readings are model readings (amendment 4), these figures measure reproducibility of the coding procedure, not agreement with a human coder, and are reported with that meaning stated.
376-104: A cell whose value does not fit its dimension, or whose quote is not verbatim in the text that was read, is flagged and sent to pass B to be re-read; it is never coerced into a permitted value, because guessing what the coder meant would put a reading into the dataset that no reader could trace to a quote. Where the coding manual itself was ambiguous it is amended, with a changelog entry, and amendments after schema freeze never rename or remove values.
376-106: Evidence-per-cell coding makes every value auditable and is what distinguishes this dataset from prior completeness matrices. Amendment 4 changes who does the verifying: no human verifies every cell, because 1,116 systems at 38 dimensions is 42,408 cells. Instead every cell carries a quote that is checked mechanically, character for character, against the exact text the coder was given, and cells that fail that check, or that fall outside their dimension's permitted values, are re-read in a repair pass and counted in the release. The rate of unresolved and non-verbatim cells is reported as a data-quality figure rather than being silently repaired.
376-110: Systems with no paper are coded from source at a pinned commit and marked primary_artifact=repo. Amendment 8: the evidence bundle presents repository excerpts without their original line numbers, so a coder cannot cite a real line. Repository locators are therefore recorded as 'path@commit' and flagged as lacking a line number; demanding a line number would only produce fabricated ones, which nothing downstream could check. The verbatim quote, verified against the exact text the coder read, is the primary evidence for each cell, and a future update will number the lines inside the bundle so cited lines can be resolved mechanically at the pinned commit.
